name: windows
title: Windows
description: Every window: stable ID, title, active, modal, size.

name: snapshot
title: Snapshot
description: The control tree as an outline: role, name, [stable ID], states, value, the actions each node takes and what its press opens (needs_user: it opens a dialog the user answers; instead= names a tool that does the same without one; default and cancel: the buttons Enter and Escape press). A virtualised list says how many rows it does not show. Narrow it with root and filter; actions false leaves the actions out. A read: needs no control.

window.description: a window's stable ID or title; default the active window

name: find
title: Find
description: Nodes by role, name (any case, part of it) and state, each with its [stable ID] and parent; cheaper than a snapshot when you know what you look for.

window.description: a window's stable ID or title; default the active window

name: act
title: Act
description: A semantic action on a node (press, select, expand, collapse, focus, set_value, increment, decrement, show_menu, close), scroll_into_view, or invoke_command on a command's stable ID. A row a virtualised list does not show is reached by its ID. A dialog you opened may be closed (close on the dialog, as Cancel), never submitted. close on a program window's own ID closes the window: save first, then close. A question the program raises during an act (save changes?) is yours and never shown: with no on_unsaved the act stops there, the program stays as it was, and the reply gives the question and its choices; on_unsaved save or discard answers it. Waits for idle and replies with what changed; terse gives counts. Acts need control: in a shared launch (--mcp-shared) your first act asks the user (a 10-second countdown that allows).

window.description: a window's stable ID or title; default the active window

target.description: a node's stable ID, or #r<n> for a runtime ID

within.description: an ancestor's stable ID, when the target's ID repeats

on_unsaved.description: The answer to a save changes? question the act raises: save or discard; without it the act stops at the question and replies with it.

name: reset
title: Reset
description: Puts the interface back in order: closes the dialogs you opened (as Cancel), popups and menus, tooltips and drags, releases pointer capture, and stops content that froze; replies with what it reset and what it left (a dialog the user opened). Acts need control: in a shared launch (--mcp-shared) your first act asks the user (a 10-second countdown that allows).

window.description: a window's stable ID or title; default the active window

name: pointer
title: Pointer
description: Pointer input through the program's own input path: move, hover, click, double_click, right_click, down, up, drag, wheel. Aim with a target (offset inside it, default its centre) or with position in window coordinates, not both. A drag presses at that point and moves through path: with a target, path points are in the target's space like offset; without one, window coordinates like position. Acts need control: in a shared launch (--mcp-shared) your first act asks the user (a 10-second countdown that allows).

window.description: a window's stable ID or title; default the active window

target.description: a node's stable ID, or #r<n> for a runtime ID

within.description: an ancestor's stable ID, when the target's ID repeats

offset.description: Logical pixels from the target's top-left corner (its bounds as snapshot bounds gives them)

position.description: Window coordinates: logical pixels from the top-left corner of the window's content area, the space of snapshot bounds

items.description: With a target, logical pixels from the target's top-left corner (as offset); without one, window coordinates (as position)

delta.description: Wheel notches: y -1 scrolls down one notch, y 1 up; x scrolls sideways. Default {x: 0, y: -1}

name: keyboard
title: Keyboard
description: Key chords ("Ctrl+S") and sequences, committed text, and composition, to the focused control or to a target focused first. Acts need control: in a shared launch (--mcp-shared) your first act asks the user (a 10-second countdown that allows). Replies with what changed, as act does.

window.description: a window's stable ID or title; default the active window

target.description: a node's stable ID, or #r<n> for a runtime ID

within.description: an ancestor's stable ID, when the target's ID repeats

name: text
title: Text
description: A node's whole text: a text control's value, selection and lines (with select, sets the selection, UTF-8 byte offsets); any other node's full name, value and description, such as a label cut in the outline.

window.description: a window's stable ID or title; default the active window

target.description: a node's stable ID, or #r<n> for a runtime ID

within.description: an ancestor's stable ID, when the target's ID repeats

name: wait
title: Wait
description: Waits until the next frame, idle, a time (ms), a condition on a node (state, value, exists) or a user step done.

window.description: a window's stable ID or title; default the active window

target.description: a node's stable ID, or #r<n> for a runtime ID

within.description: an ancestor's stable ID, when the target's ID repeats

name: capture
title: Capture
description: A window or control as a PNG, drawn fresh from the current state; a window's open popup windows (menus, drop-downs) and its tooltip window are composited over it unless popups is false. Password fields are painted out. The in-use sign (the band, AI mode's stripes) is left out unless include_sign is true, so you see the program as its user does without a model. points [{x, y}, ...] (or [x, y] pairs; logical units from the captured area's top left, at most 1024) answers the colour at each instead of an image, to check a drawing cheaply. path saves the PNG to a file and replies with its path, size and dimensions (the command folder, given no path, saves to capture-<n>.png in its own folder). A read: needs no control.

window.description: a window's stable ID or title; default the active window

target.description: a node's stable ID, or #r<n> for a runtime ID

within.description: an ancestor's stable ID, when the target's ID repeats

path.description: Save the PNG to this file (an absolute path ending .png) and reply with its path, size and dimensions instead of the image

overwrite.description: Replace a file already at path

name: inspect
title: Inspect
description: Beyond accessibility, sections chosen with what: state, layout, paint, metrics, dispatcher, interaction, session, schema, clipboard, summary, layout_reasons, resources, events. With a target, state, layout and schema by default; without, metrics, dispatcher and interaction.

window.description: a window's stable ID or title; default the active window

target.description: a node's stable ID, or #r<n> for a runtime ID

within.description: an ancestor's stable ID, when the target's ID repeats

name: batch
title: Batch
description: Several steps in one call with one combined reply: each step is {"tool": name, ...that tool's arguments} or an expect guard {"expect": "node"|"visual", target, state, value, exists, drawn}; the batch stops at the first failure or unmet expectation; at most 512 steps. terse gives each act's changes as counts.

items.description: a tool step {tool, ...that tool's arguments} or an expect step {expect, window, target, within, state, value, exists, drawn}

window.description: a window's stable ID or title; default the active window

target.description: a node's stable ID, or #r<n> for a runtime ID

within.description: an ancestor's stable ID, when the target's ID repeats

state.description: a state the node has, or -state for one it lacks

drawn.description: visual: whether the state is drawn

name: release_control
title: Release control
description: Gives the program back to the user and ends AI mode. In a --mcp-shared launch your first act asks the user (a 10-second countdown that allows when it ends) and you then hold control until you release it or 30 s pass without a call; in a --mcp-fcfs launch your first act takes control at once and you keep it until you release it or the user takes it back. Reads never need control.

name: close
title: Close
description: Quits the program: every program window is asked to close, as the user's quit does. An act: it takes control first as any act does in this launch (at once under --mcp-fcfs; under --mcp-shared the user may refuse). A question the program raises (save changes?) is yours and never shown: with no on_unsaved nothing closes and the reply names it; on_unsaved save or discard answers it. Unlike disconnect, which ends your session (and, with mode hard, closes), close is about the program.

window.description: a window's stable ID or title; default the active window

on_unsaved.description: The answer to a save changes? question the act raises: save or discard; without it the act stops at the question and replies with it.

name: disconnect
title: Disconnect
description: Ends your session and closes the program cleanly. An act: it takes control first as any act does in this launch (under --mcp-shared the user may refuse, and the program stays open). The usual path: save your work with the program's save tool, then disconnect. mode soft (the default) never closes over unsaved work and never shows anything: if the program asks to save, nothing closes, and the reply names what to save; save it, then disconnect again. mode hard ends the session regardless: control returns to the user and the program's own save question is shown to the user, or, with discard_unsaved true, unsaved changes are discarded and nothing is asked.
